summary: Reserved GPU cluster: sustained tail-latency spike and intermittent 504s during overlapping offline scoring jobs
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 10:10 UTC, CartaOps reported elevated tail latencies (p95/p99) and intermittent 504 timeouts observed by their production service backed by a Dedicated GPU pool in us-west. Impact: customer reports increased end-user request failures and delayed responses for multi-turn chat endpoints; business impact is material for CartaOps' paid workload. Environment: Dedicated pool (4 x A100 GPUs reserved), autoscaler configured with instance-based thresholds (scale up at 70% avg GPU util), running redwood-rlhf-v2-13b as primary model for heavy scoring traffic. Observed behavior: p95 increased from ~120ms to 700-1200ms at peak, p99 breached 3s leading to client-side 504s. Spikes are correlated with nightly offline scoring jobs (large batch requests) that overlap with peak live traffic window. Expected behavior: stable p95 < 200ms and <1% 5xx/timeout rate for dedicated tier under committed baseline throughput.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route a steady stream of concurrent chat inference requests (QPS ~ 40) to customer's dedicated pool using redwood-rlhf-v2-13b.
2) Kick off an offline scoring job that streams large batching requests (bulk scoring using batch_size ~ 1024) targeting the same pool at T+5 minutes.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency metrics and request error rates in the Redwood Console; reproduce increased queuing and occasional 504s after the batch job overlaps with live traffic.
4) Repeat with autoscaler set to current thresholds (scale up at 70% avg GPU util) to see delayed scaling behavior and transient GPU memory pressure reports.

investigation_notes: Initial triage by support (Aisha): correlated customer error reports with elevated queue depth and GPU memory utilization spikes in the dedicated pool around 10:10-10:30 UTC.

SRE (Daniel) hypothesis 1: autoscaler threshold and aggregation window are too coarse; by the time scale-up completes, background batch jobs have saturated GPU memory and PCIe bandwidth, causing head-of-line waiting for interactive requests.

SRE hypothesis 2: batch job launcher is using aggressive packing affinity causing multiple large batches to be scheduled on same physical GPU nodes (noisy neighbor effect), exacerbating cache eviction and KV-cache cold misses for interactive inference.

Observability finding: node-level metrics show transient increases in PCIe bandwidth and GPU memory utilization near 100% during incidents; pod-level logs show repeated soft OOM warnings and queued requests kept waiting in serving-runtime for >800ms.
Checked linked tickets: SUP-31845 (gpu-evictions) has similar pattern but different root cause; referencing it for mitigation ideas.
Temporary mitigation applied: paused customer-scheduled offline scoring batch windows for 30 minutes; this reduced p99 to <1.2s and eliminated new 504s while we continued analysis.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T10:25Z: Reached out to CartaOps (CSM) to request a hold on scheduled batch scoring while we investigate. Customer agrees to pause for 30 minutes.

Daniel Kim (SRE) 2026-03-12T10:40Z: Observed co-scheduling of batch pods on same nodes as inference pods; adding immediate node taint rule to prevent fresh batch jobs from landing on dedicated inference nodes (temp).

Leah Chen (Solutions Eng) 2026-03-12T11:05Z: Suggested short-term config change: lower autoscaler scale-up threshold to 55% avg GPU util and shorten aggregation window to 30s to allow faster reaction to batch-induced load.

CartaOps (Customer) 2026-03-12T11:20Z: Confirmed improved response times after pause; reported one residual 504 during the mitigation window. Asked for long-term solution to avoid scheduling collisions.
resolution_notes: Mitigation 1 (applied 2026-03-12T10:45Z): Pause scheduled offline scoring jobs for CartaOps and apply temporary taint rule to prefer inference-only nodes. Result: immediate drop in new 504s and lower p99 latency.

Mitigation 2 (applied 2026-03-12T11:00Z): Adjust autoscaler policy for this customer's dedicated pool: scale_up_threshold -> 55%, scale_up_window -> 30s, scale_up_cooldown -> 120s. Observed faster scale events and reduced queuing.

Permanent fix plan: implement scheduler-level isolation for dedicated inference pools to prevent batch scheduling on inference nodes; add autoscaler policy profile per-customer for mixed workloads; augment telemetry to alert on PCIe saturation and KV-cache miss rate.
Customer rollback and verification: CartaOps confirmed their nightly batch window was rescheduled to a non-overlapping window and requested SLOs be documented.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering to deliver scheduler change to mark dedicated inference nodes as 'inference-only' for batch job placement (ENG-1421). Target: 2026-03-26.
2) Autoscaler team to introduce per-pool scaling profiles and faster reaction path for p95-sensitive pools (ENG-1499). Target: 2026-03-19.
3) Observability: add PCIe bandwidth and GPU soft-oom alerts to pool dashboard and create an automated runbook link when thresholds breach (OPS-88).
4) Update Customer Runbook for CartaOps: recommended throughput per model, batch-window scheduling guidelines, and a contact for emergency pauses.
